prompt:
A full-fidelity desktop website homepage design comp, landscape, shown flat with no browser frame and no device. This is the website of a Christian nonprofit that provides reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost. Layout, top to bottom:

1. NAVIGATION BAR (thin, full width) on a pale clear-glass ivory ground: at left a text wordmark "Beauty From Ashes" in a dignified serif with "SURGICAL MINISTRY" in small spaced capitals below it; centered links "Our Mission", "How We Help", "Stories", "Get Involved", "Contact"; at right a small "EN | ES" language switch and a solid amber-gold button "Give". A thick dark graphite lead line runs under the bar.

2. HERO (about 60% of the height), split by a vertical dark lead line:
- LEFT 45%: a pane of clear, faintly textured cathedral glass in warm ivory. Small spaced-capitals eyebrow: "A CHRISTIAN SURGICAL MINISTRY · CHARLOTTE & FORT MILL". A large near-black serif headline over three lines: "Restoring more than what can be seen." A short paragraph: "Reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost, for children and adults whose need exceeds their means. Open to everyone." Two buttons: a solid amber-gold glass button "Ask for help" and a dark outlined button "Refer someone".
- RIGHT 55%: a tall modern abstract leaded stained-glass window, the page's single dominant visual. Large geometric and gently curving panes of deep cobalt blue, midnight navy, amber gold, honey, and clear seedy glass, joined by thick dark graphite lead cames; antique glass with visible bubbles, streaks and subtle color variation; lit from behind by warm daylight so the amber and cobalt glow. Purely abstract: no human figures, no crosses, no doves, no sunsets, no religious scenes.

3. VALUES BAND (bottom 30%): the window's lead lines continue across the page and divide a horizontal row of six equal panes. Above the row, small spaced capitals "THEREFORE". Each pane holds a serif heading and one line of small sans text: "We Listen." / "We give every patient the time their story deserves." — "We Protect." / "We hold patient safety as our highest surgical standard." — "We Pray." / "We pray with every patient who welcomes it." — "We Accompany." / "We walk with every patient long after surgery ends." — "We Honor." / "We honor the sacrifice behind every patient's decision." — "We Serve." / "We extend surgical care where need exceeds means." Most panes are clear ivory glass with dark text; one is deep cobalt glass with ivory text.

Overall: calm, dignified, professional, warm and hopeful; unmistakably a real nonprofit website with crisp, legible web typography. Strong dark lead lines are the layout grid; color lives in large glass fields rather than decoration. Not a church bulletin, not a cosmetic surgery advertisement.
